messages:
sophia: quick heads-up — ran an *SQ + act-aware* pass on 48k tokens for the new rdx-7b-long model, and saw a weird accuracy glitch around KV-cache boundaries.
ajay: ok what's the glitch look like? numbers?
sophia: overall MRR is fine at +0.2%, but when sequences cross cache chunk boundaries the F1 on long-span coref drops ~3.5% on our eval set.
irene: is this repeatable on single-run vs batched runs?
sophia: yes, repros on single-worker single-stream, but magnitude depends on batch size. batch_size=1 -> ~2.8% drop, batch_size=8 -> ~3.9% drop.
matt: did you check layerwise activations? sounds like act-scale mismatch in some transformer blocks.
sophia: I dumped per-layer act scale stats. pattern: middle attention layers (6-9) have a skewed RMS increase right after the 16k token mark. here's the short log snippet:

```
# act_rms per layer (sample)
layer 5: 0.82 -> 0.84
layer 6: 0.91 -> 1.24  <-- spike post-16k
layer 7: 0.88 -> 1.10
layer 8: 0.94 -> 1.28  <-- spike
layer 9: 0.79 -> 0.81
```

sophia: these spikes correlate with increased quantization error in AWQ/SQ paths.
ajay: interesting. Were you using the same cross-layer scale for SmoothQuant or per-layer act-scale?
sophia: per-layer, but smoothing window is global (n=256). trying per-layer adaptive window now.
irene: any diff between AWQ vs GPTQ for those layers?
sophia: GPTQ keeps those layers much closer to fp32 (<=0.6% drop), AWQ+SQ shows the biggest regression.
matt: could be due to attention softmax dynamic range shifting when key/value caches are concatenated across chunks.
bench-bot: benchmark run 1923456794: rdx-7b-long 48k, batch=8, awq-sq: latency 220ms/token, cpu mem spike on chunk boundary +150MB
ajay: cpu mem spike suggests memcpy + concat is creating transient scale differences. maybe KV cache padding introduces zeros that change batch-normed stats.
sophia: to isolate: I ran var-free concat (no zero padding), and the reg drop reduces to ~1.2%.
irene: so padding is a culprit. can we do runtime strip-and-append to avoid zero-insertion?
ajay: yes but that adds branching; might hurt throughput. alternative: maintain per-chunk act-statistics and apply a small per-chunk correction factor before quantization.
matt: another idea: for deployment, mark attention KV layers as "quant-fallback" for AWQ path, keep GPTQ/FP8 for them. rest use SQ-AWQ.
sophia: perf tradeoff: marking 2 layers as fallback increases cost ~4% but restores accuracy.
bench-bot: quick config diff I tested:

```
--quant-profile: smoothquant
--act-aware: true
--fallback-layers: [6,8]
--batching: continuous-prefix
```

sophia: results with that config: MRR delta -> -0.1% (vs fp32), latency +3.8%.
irene: that's acceptable for dedicated customers. for hosted we should offer an automatic policy: try aggressive sq, run eval on a short prompt set, if fallbacks needed toggle per-layer.
ajay: agree. we can implement a cheap eval hook in the bring-up pipeline that runs 500 short long-context samples and computes per-layer act-deltas.
matt: also add a small fuzz test that simulates chunk-boundary padding to the eval corpus.
sophia: ticketed next steps:
- (sophia) add per-chunk act-stat dump to quantize job (PR later today)
- (ajay) prototype per-layer fallback flag + auto-eval hook
- (irene) measure perf delta on Dedicated nodes (A100-80GB) and on shared hosted pool
- (matt) add chunk-padding fuzz cases to onboarding eval

ajay: can we also try dynamic smoothing (reduce window after chunk boundary) as a lightweight mitigation?
sophia: will try. quick note: quantize command I used:

```
python tools/quantize.py --model rdx-7b-long --algo awq --smoothquant --act-window 256 --evalset longcoref-1k --batch 8
```

matt: thanks — keep logs here. if fallback rule looks stable we can add to model card: "prefer GPTQ for attention layers when using AWQ+SQ on >32k contexts".
sophia: uploading per-layer dumps to gs://redwood-ml/sq-run-1923456789/
bench-bot: upload complete: gs://redwood-ml/sq-run-1923456789/artifacts.tar.gz
ajay: good work. will sync with infra about making the eval hook part of bring-up pipeline.
irene: leaving a small reminder to document the user-facing perf/accuracy tradeoffs for the Console rollout.
sophia: thanks — will follow up with PR and a short note in model onboarding checklist. :thumbsup:
